_comment: The whole quest. Node ids here are authoring names; the generator assigns numeric graph ids. Links are [from, to] or [from, to, input_socket]; either endpoint may be written 'node:Socket' - journal nodes need the input socket named because the socket IS the state transition, and condition nodes need the output socket named because they branch on True/False. One socket may carry several connections: on an output that is a parallel fan-out, on an input it is an OR-join.
_phase_revision: Bump this to force the phase to re-enter on a save that has already run it. ArchiveXL names the questPhaseNodeDefinition it builds in the parent quest CRC16(phase depot path + ':' + parent node id), derives a fact id from that node id, and on every load force-starts the node only when that fact is still 0 - then sets it to 1 whether or not anything actually ran. A save that loaded a broken build therefore carries a permanent 'already started' marker for that exact path. Changing the revision changes the depot filename, so the CRC, the node id and the fact id are all new and the phase starts cleanly. Verified against cp2077-archive-xl/src/App/Extensions/QuestPhase/Extension.cpp (PatchPhase, OnGameRestored, CreatePhaseNode, GeneratePhaseNodeID). See D21. Bumped to 19 on 2026-09-22 (D127). D126 inserted five nodes near the TOP of the node array and gen_questphase numbers nodes by their position in it, so every id after them moved; a save parked mid-phase against r18 would have resumed against the wrong numbering. The bump is safe because every side effect in this graph sits behind a guard that reads a fact the player already has - tools/replaytest.py proves a re-entry fires none of them - and because guard_hook now also tests ashcache_progress == 0, so the re-walk rings the opening call only for a player who had not started the quest yet. r20 (2026-09-24, D134): the D133 probe branch removed; saves that ran r19 hold probe_prefab_wait active. r21 (2026-09-25, D158): terminal branch forked off desc_find_box, joined by wait_terminal; a save parked at take_chip had already passed the fork, so it needs the re-walk to start the terminal. r22 (2026-09-26, D171): re-walk used to replay the Mara meeting in a save with ashcache_mara_choice_made reset to 0, to see the new idle workspot; no node change. r23 (2026-10-02): temporary questShowWorldNode door-test branch; every load crashed (3/3). r24 (2026-10-02): branch removed, r22 graph under a new id to bisect the crash.

nodes._comment: The socket name is load-bearing and is NOT free choice. ArchiveXL builds a questPhaseNodeDefinition inside the parent quest for us and hardcodes its entry socket as In1 (the literal is in ArchiveXL.dll, and every injected phase on this machine - lifeswitch, llquest_root, vendorsxl_*, uqs_launcher - names it In1). The engine enters a child phase by matching that socket name against a questInputNodeDefinition here. Name it anything else and the phase merges, resolves, and never runs a single node - silently.
Entry gate. Set by the redscript glue once the start conditions are met; also the hook a CET debug command uses to force-start the quest.

The phone leads and the journal follows, which is the order every vanilla side job arrives in: something buzzes, you read it, and only then does a new entry appear in the log. This used to fire first, so the quest announced itself and then explained why - the right beats in the wrong order, and it read as a mod handing out a task rather than as somebody contacting V.

=== The hook (D126). The quest used to open with two SMS from an unknown number; it opens with a call from the same number now. The slot is unchanged - still between await_start and quest_active, so the phone still leads and the journal still follows, which is the order every vanilla side job arrives in.

The guard is new and is not decoration. Two journal_entry nodes needed none: re-activating a message that is already in the thread shows the player nothing. A call re-fires audibly. A phase_revision bump re-walks a finished save from the top, and without this the opening hook rings again hours into the quest, explaining a burn order the player has already beaten.

Opens the phone. applyPhoneRestriction is off here and ON at the hang-up, which is not a typo - phoneSystem.script's TriggerCall only touches the restriction when the flag is 1, and on the EndCall branch it calls ApplyPhoneCallRestriction(FALSE), so 1 on EndCall is what RELEASES the phone. Vanilla ships exactly this pair; see D124 and q112_03_infiltration.

Audio, not Video: the caller is anonymous, and a video call would put a face in the corner of the screen that this quest has decided never to show.

source/scene_hookcall.json. 'anchor' pins it to the player rather than to a marker, and here that is not a convenience but a requirement: this fires 30 real seconds after Somewhat Damaged ends (see source/glue.json 'start'), and V can be anywhere in Night City when it does. A scene anchored at the clinic would be a scene that may simply never play - and the quest's only objective is raised at the end of it.
Hangs up and gives the phone back. See hook_start on why this one carries the restriction flag.

After the hang-up, never before the ring. A save interrupted mid-call then rings again rather than losing the address - and at this point in the quest the address IS the quest, because no objective has been raised yet.

Activates this objective's description paragraph, the block the journal screen shows above the objective list. It is a separate entry - gameJournalQuestDescription, id 'description', a child of the objective - and it needs activating in its own right. QuestLogUtils.UnpackRecursiveWithFilter skips every entry whose own state is Inactive and exempts only JournalQuestMapPinBase, so before this node existed all 12 descriptions were written, localized, shipped in the resource, and filtered out of GetDescriptions - an empty panel with nothing logged anywhere. Retires this paragraph as the objective closes. questLogDetailsPanel.PopulateObjectives concatenates EVERY description GetDescriptions returns into the one m_questDescription text field, and a Succeeded objective is still walked - GetDescriptions' own filter sets succeeded=true, and the recursion into an objective re-enters with GetDefaultFilter(), which accepts Active children. So a description that is never set Inactive keeps rendering for the rest of the quest. The separator is a single space, not a paragraph break: the line 'description + "\n";' under the concatenation discards its result and is dead code in the shipped script. Without these nodes the panel grows into one run-on blob of every paragraph so far, and a phase_revision re-entry produces the whole blob at once because the walk races through every already-set pause_fact in a single frame. Vanilla sidesteps it by carrying few descriptions - Hot Fuzz ships two, 'description' and 'judy_notell', both on its only objective - while this quest carries one per objective, so it retires them instead. The four ending descriptions are deliberately NOT retired: they are what a finished quest shows in the log.

=== ACT 3: the box, then Mara. meet_mara plays source/scene_mara.json, which sets ashcache_mara_choice_made and, on the two non-hostile routes, ashcache_mara_trusted. Those facts are set INSIDE the scene by embedded scnQuestNodes, so the graph does not wait on them - the scene node itself blocks until the conversation ends (decision D1). The box works the same way since D102: open_box plays source/scene_box.json, whose only content is a Use hub attached to the Relic case, and the scene node blocks until V presses it. This guard is what a second entry into the phase (a phase_revision bump) reads, so a save that already opened the box is not asked to open it again. The set_fact after the scene is what keeps ashcache_box_opened honest for everything that reads it - the dev report, the glue's stage arming, and a later save that jumps in behind this point.

Both routes out of guard_splinter arrive here, which is why it takes two connections on one input socket: the run that just took the splinter, and a re-entry walk that finds it already taken.

Which door of the Mara scene to open. The fourth micro-choice quotes her journal back at her, so it may only be offered to a player who read the shard - and an option cannot be greyed out - it can now be conditioned (D26), but a failing condition removes it rather than dimming it (see the header of source/scene_mara.json, and D14 for the same move on the ending). So the gate is a graph branch and the scene has two entry points. ashcache_journal_read is set by the redscript shard hook, so it is genuinely readable by the time V walks in; a player who reads the shard AFTER this node fires gets the three-option hub, which is the same one-shot behaviour route_hide has and is correct - the conversation has already started.

nodes._location: The scene has no position of its own; this NodeRef is its origin - everything in the scene is placed relative to it. Defined as a worldStaticMarkerNode in source/world.json (sector ash_cache_clinic). The LONG form is deliberate: a map pin resolves the short '#ac_mara' fine, but the only observed sceneLocation sample uses the full path, and a scene anchored to nothing plays at the world origin instead of erroring.

nodes._comment: Interruption safety net. Required because ash_cache_mara.scene raises the gameplay tier: if the player is interrupted out of a Tier3 conversation and nothing hands control back, they are left unable to move, with no error anywhere. Every one of the 15 wired INT paths in the shipped game is this exact shape - 500 ms realtime delay, then questSetTier to Tier1_FullGameplay - and 13 of 128 interruption-aware phases bother to wire it at all, because only the ones that change tier have to. See reference/interruption.md and D28.
Return half of the same net - see the INT comment above.

count 1 per spawner: each NodeRef addresses one NPC, so 'this one is down' is GreaterOrEqual 1. defeated/killed/unconscious all count, so a non-lethal build finishes the fight too.

=== ACT 5b: Mara comes out (D123). Sits between the fight closing and the D3 hide gate, so she speaks BEFORE the decision rather than after it - which is the whole point of the beat: what she says reframes the choice V is about to make. Plays source/scene_aftertalk.json.

Two conditions, cheapest first, both of which mean 'skip it entirely': she has to be alive, and this has to be the first time. mara_dead is 0 on every route the graph can currently produce - protect_mara makes her Immortal and never releases it - but the gate is written anyway, for the same reason gate_hide writes it: the day a branch can kill her, nothing here needs revisiting. mara_warned is set inside the scene, on both of its routes, so the guard is 1 for exactly the players who finished it - the same shape guard_meet_mara uses on ashcache_mara_choice_made, and the reason a phase_revision bump cannot yank the player back into a Tier3 conversation.

Picks which door of the scene to open, exactly as route_mara and route_hide do. False is the intimidate route, which gets its own four lines and no choice hub. She hands over Cynosure either way - see the header of source/scene_aftertalk.json for why that is deliberate and not an oversight.

'She emerges from the clinic' is therefore a property of this one line: no new position to stand on, and nothing to measure.

D120. The beat each ending was missing, one node per ending. They all play source/scene_epilogue.json and differ only in which door they open: three entry points, three exit points, and the three beats inside never see each other. Three nodes rather than one shared node with three entries because a shared one would hand the graph three live exit sockets from a single walk - which is also exactly what tools/replaytest.py reported. Anchored to #ac_clinic_entrance, the verified marker decide_scene uses (D9): the decision hands straight over to this and V has not moved.

D120 re-entry guards, one per ending, on the same fact. A phase_revision bump re-walks a FINISHED save from 'start', and every fact it reads is still set, so the walk races through the whole quest and arrives back at its own ending - replaying the beat, taking an item the player no longer has, and in the Blue Eyes case paying 15,000 eddies a second time. False skips straight to the objective's Succeeded socket, so the spine is unchanged either way. Same shape as guard_splinter; measured by tools/replaytest.py (D50).

D120. Three of the four endings END WITH THE SPLINTER GONE - burned, read into a head, or dropped in somebody else's box - and until now all three left it sitting in the backpack afterwards. The chip tree does not notice: its visibility is keyed on the fact ashcache_splinter_given, not on holding the item, so the perks V bought with it survive the object leaving.

D120. 'For a price' made literal. Items.money is the game's own currency item - the same TweakDB id vanilla loot and every eddies mod moves - so the engine raises its normal eddies notification on the grant and no HUD node is needed. notify is on because this one IS the payoff.

D120. The receipt, on the same anonymous thread that pushed V at the courier in Act 1. Fired after the scene hands control back, so the phone buzzes in normal gameplay rather than over a Tier3 conversation, next to the eddies notification.

D120. Set last in every ending chain, after the beat has played and its side effects have landed, so a save taken mid-beat replays it rather than skipping it. One fact for all three: they are mutually exclusive and the guard only ever asks 'has an ending already played'.

D121. The fourth epilogue door. D120 built three and left Hide on the build-1 treatment - objective raised, objective completed, splinter still in the backpack - which left the one ending gated on Mara's trust as the one ending she does not appear in. Same guard fact and same shape as the other three.
Buried with the case. The same defect D120 fixed on the other three endings and did not fix here: 'bury the case where the FIA does not look' ticked with the splinter still in V's pocket.
All five paths OR-join on this one Succeeded socket.

D121. Mara's verdict on what V did with the splinter, wired at the point all four endings already converge rather than four times over inside them. Chained on False exactly like the ending switch above it (br_destroy -> br_absorb -> br_hide), and reading the same ashcache_end_* facts, so the two switches cannot disagree about which ending happened.

False is the intimidate route and it short-circuits the whole chain: she sends one message, the same four lines whatever V chose. That sameness is the characterisation - she is squaring a debt with a stranger, not reacting to a friend's decision.
The only one of the four where she is frightened rather than relieved or disappointed, and the only one that asks V for something back.

Tested rather than assumed as the last else, for the reason br_hide gives: a False here means no ending fact was set at all, which is a bug and not a player choice. It routes on to the break check with no message rather than sending the wrong woman's reaction to an ending that did not happen.

The payoff for opt_break_j - until now the hardest option in Mara's conversation set a fact alongside trust and nothing ever read it. Last in the chain so it arrives after whichever verdict she sent, which is what makes it read as an afterthought she could not help sending. Unreachable on the intimidate route by construction: break is only ever set alongside trusted.

=== ACT 7b: the holocall (D124). Mara rings V once the ending has landed and hands over the Cynosure address - the payoff for after_close_1, 'Keep the phone on. One day you'll want the address.'

Placed HERE, between the ending messages and the landfill aftermath, for two reasons. It has to be after the endings because what she is calling about is what V just did with the splinter; and it has to be before the aftermath because on the absorb and blueeyes routes the aftermath is where she turns up dead. A call from a woman whose body the player has already found would be a bug that reads as a ghost story.

Three tests. mara_dead is the fight; mara_warned is the promise itself, and reading it rather than mara_trusted is what lets the intimidate route get the call too - she gave V the address on that route as well, just with worse grace. mara_called is the replay guard.

Opens the phone. applyPhoneRestriction is left off here and switched ON at the hang-up, which is not a typo: phoneSystem.script's TriggerCall only touches the restriction when the flag is 1, and on the EndCall branch it calls ApplyPhoneCallRestriction(FALSE). So 1 on EndCall is what RELEASES the phone. Vanilla ships exactly this pair - see q112_03_infiltration, Takemura twice.

The conversation itself. 'anchor' pins it to the player rather than to a marker, because by now V could be anywhere in Night City and a scene anchored at the clinic is a scene that may never get to play. No INT/RET net is wired: this scene raises no tier, so there is no gameplay state for an interruption to restore.

'every_ending' is read by tools/replaytest.py only. It says this beat runs whichever ending the player took, so the tool stops counting it once per ending and reporting 4x. Nothing else in the graph claims it, and anything that claims it by accident would be hiding a guard that has stopped reading the ending.
Hangs up and gives the phone back. See holo_start on why this one carries the restriction flag.

Set after the hang-up rather than before the ring, so a save interrupted mid-call rings again rather than losing the address forever. Same rule every replay guard in this graph follows: the marker goes immediately after the effect it guards, never before.

=== ACT 8: the aftermath (D122). Everything below sits between the ending messages and quest_done, so the quest is still OPEN while the landfill objective is up - an objective raised after gameJournalQuest fires Succeeded would be an objective on a completed quest, which the journal UI has no place to draw. The cost is that a player who never drives out there leaves one thread open forever, which is a fair description of the ending anyway.

Three conditions decide whether there is a body at all, cheapest first. She turns up dead in exactly the two endings that leave the cache ALIVE in the world - absorb, where it is in V's head, and blueeyes, where V sold the trail with it. Burn it or bury it and nobody has a reason to go looking for her. Nothing in the text ever says this; it is meant to be found by comparing saves.
She already died in the clinic - there is no landfill beat, and the Hide ending was locked out for the same reason (gate_hide). Falls through.

D122. Retire the ending's own description before raising the landfill one. An ending description is never switched off anywhere else - it stays Active until the quest closes, which was invisible while it was the only live paragraph. The aftermath adds a second, and the log panel concatenates every still-Active description into ONE field (D54), so absorb plus landfill would have rendered as a single run-on block. tools/descpanel.py caught it.

D127. The aftermath used to reach Blue Eyes by elimination: not hide, not destroy, not absorb, therefore blueeyes, therefore Mara turns up dead. That made 'she is dead' the DEFAULT outcome of the whole chain - any state in which no ending fact is set at all reads as the one ending that kills her, and the player is shown a body for a choice they did not make. A positive test costs one node and removes the whole class.

Appended at the end of the nodes array rather than written beside route_body_absorb on purpose: gen_questphase numbers nodes by their position in this list (enumerate(specs)), so inserting one in the middle renumbers every node after it and a save parked mid-phase would resume against the wrong ids. Position in this array is not meaning - the links below are what wire the graph.

D128. The counterweight to open_clinic_entrance. The quest used to ForceOpen this door in act 2 and never touch it again, so Farida's clinic stood open for the rest of the save - including for q303/q304, the Phantom Liberty mission that dresses this same prefab and installs V's facial implant there. Closing it when the quest starts means the quest owns the door for exactly its own duration: shut at the opening call, opened on arrival, left open afterwards. Appended to the end of the nodes array, never inserted: gen_questphase numbers nodes by position, so an insertion would renumber every node after it.

ForceLock rather than relying on the close alone: DoorControllerPS.OnQuestForceClose (vanilla_scripts.reds:135551) sets isOpened false and leaves isLocked untouched, and an unlocked vanilla door opens on approach - which is the 'can be freely entered' the close was supposed to stop. Order matters only in that ForceLock does not reopen: close first, then lock. Both are undone in one call by the act 2 ForceOpen (:135528 sets opened, unlocked, unsealed).

The inner double door, closed for the same reason and at the same moment as the street door. Symmetry with the open pair is the invariant worth keeping: whatever this quest shuts, the same two ForceOpen nodes reopen.
Locked with the entrance so the pair is reversed exactly by the pair that opens it.
